diagnoses.label: Deliverables and completion conditions not enumerated
diagnoses.observable_evidence: reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md ends with 'Sanity checks' and a scaffold that writes 'into /app/output' but never names q01.json–q05.json, their schemas, or a 'done when all five are present and schema-valid' completion gate. The 'When to invoke' and 'Output construction guardrails' sections talk about rounding/sorting but omit the file-level deliverables manifest that the task spec requires.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies to reflow profile compliance runs that must emit a fixed set of per-question JSON files under /app/output (q01.json … q05.json) with specified schemas.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not turn this into per-question solution logic or hardcode handbook values; keep it a file/schema/completion contract only.
diagnoses.target_section: Output construction guardrails / Minimal end-to-end scaffold (add an explicit 'Deliverables & completion' subsection)
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Add a deliverables manifest that enumerates the five output paths (/app/output/q01.json … q05.json), restates each required top-level schema shape at a contract level (keys, sort order, null policy), and defines completion as 'all five files written, schema-valid, sorted, 2dp-rounded, no NaN/Inf'. Keep existing sanity checks and computation recipes untouched.

diagnoses.label: Q02 representative thermocouple selection rule ambiguous for TAL
diagnoses.observable_evidence: Section 4 'Deterministic sensor selection' lumps TAL into the minimum-metric case with '(min_value, smallest_tc_id)' and the example comment '"coldest" TAL or peak', but Q02's output requires exactly one tc_id/tal_s per run and the handbook convention for TAL is to pick the worst-case (shortest TAL) sensor as representative. The current wording is ambiguous about whether 'coldest' means lowest temperature TC or shortest TAL, and does not tie Q02's single-TC emission to a specific rule.
diagnoses.scope_boundary: Applies only to Q02-style TAL reduction where one tc_id and one tal_s must be reported per run_id against handbook min/max TAL window.
diagnoses.do_not_generalize_to: Do not change ramp (Q01) or peak (Q03) selection rules, and do not alter the time_above_threshold_s interpolation routine.
diagnoses.target_section: Section 4 'Deterministic sensor selection (tie-breaks)' plus a Q02-specific note in the deliverables section
diagnoses.recommended_direction: Disambiguate the TAL case: state that the representative TC for TAL is the worst-case sensor as defined by the handbook's 'cold spot / worst case / representative sensor' guidance (i.e., the TC with the minimum TAL after per-TC computation), with (min tal_s, smallest tc_id) as the deterministic tie-break. Explicitly separate this from peak's 'coldest peak' rule so Q02 and Q03 selection logic are not conflated.

overlay.composition_issue: The missing deliverables contract and the ambiguous Q02 sensor-selection rule interact: without a per-file schema contract, the ambiguity in TAL representative-TC selection cannot be deterministically enforced at writeback. Fixing the manifest provides the slot where the TAL selection rule must be referenced, and tightening Section 4 provides the mechanism that the manifest cites.
preservation_constraints: Keep the handbook 'where to look' checklist and cfg object schema unchanged.
Preserve max_slope_in_temp_band and time_above_threshold_s implementations verbatim.
Preserve rounding helper r2, sort order rules, and NaN/Inf null policy.
Preserve Q01 ramp max-metric tie-break (max_value, smallest tc_id) and Q03 peak min-metric semantics.
Preserve conveyor feasibility rule-object patterns and the 'When to invoke' triggers.
Do not modify the companion skill reflow-machine-maintenance-guidance/SKILL.md or reference.md.

package_assessment.rationale: Both defects localize to editable prose sections of reflow-profile-compliance-toolkit/SKILL.md (output/deliverables guardrails and the Section 4 sensor-selection rule). No binary assets, external retrieval, or cross-skill changes are required; the companion skill and reference.md remain untouched.
